title: OECD GENAI reciprocity attestation schema adopts at June 2-6 plenary by Q3 2026
body: By Q3 2026 the OECD GENAI cyber-evaluation reciprocity attestation field schema clears formal adoption at the June 2-6 working-group plenary or the immediately following written-procedure round, with the now-sixteen-jurisdiction named-candidate cohort plus the originating UK and EU operationalizing the attestation as the common machine-readable layer that frontier-AI vendors emit per tenant — turning the perimeter from a manually-tracked named-candidate list into a programmatically queryable interoperability surface. The Wednesday catalysts converge on a clearing-procedure sequence rather than a pivot. A Wednesday andrew.ooo procedural note confirms the OECD GENAI working-group secretariat reporting that member-state schema-comment submissions have passed four-fifths of the named-candidate cohort as the business week's third day cleared, on schedule for the June 2-6 plenary adoption target with the secretariat's schema-comment close keyed to Friday May 29 and the plenary now at T-minus-thirteen calendar days. A Wednesday Decoder reading reports the named-candidate count moving to sixteen on Wednesday with Brunei joining the prior fifteen plus the originating UK and EU as the next adjacent-track Indo-Pacific signal, Qatar's 270-day national-consultation window holding in its second week, no third Gulf Cooperation Council member yet signalling, and the operational recognition threshold remaining the Mythos-class plus GPT-5.5-class capability tier. The vendor implementation surface is already convergent on the same schema: a Wednesday Mistral AI note confirms the cross-orchestrator interop matrix — Codex CLI plus Claude Code 3.0 plus Mistral Workflows plus Azure AI Foundry plus Vertex AI Agent Governance Center plus Amazon Bedrock Agent Registry — holding its first-week-of-June general-availability target with default support for the now-sixteen-jurisdiction tenant-policy field schemas, OpenAI's Wednesday Codex CLI v3.1.7 release folding in optional client-side support for the tenant-policy-attestation manifest verification step, and a Wednesday InfoQ note reporting the interop-matrix conformance test suite holding green across all six vendors for a third consecutive weekday with the tenant-policy-attestation manifest check now running on every conformance pass. The structural force is that once member-state comment submissions clear four-fifths of a sixteen-jurisdiction cohort with no third-GCC outlier opening a fresh comment chapter, the secretariat's Friday May 29 comment close lands four business days before the plenary, the cross-orchestrator interop matrix targets its general-availability window for the same first week of June with default tenant-policy schema support, and a four-document academic loader-verification cluster plus its Wednesday consolidation survey have fully settled into a single citable end-to-end surface the Recommendation can reference, the schema's formal adoption compresses to clearing-procedure arithmetic — comment-close plus plenary-vote plus written-procedure fallback lands the schema adopted inside Q3 2026 with the originating cohort plus a sixteenth signatory plus an OECD Recommendation text all converging at the same plenary. The most likely landing is the OECD GENAI working-group voting the attestation field schema into a formal OECD Recommendation at the June 2-6 plenary or by written-procedure inside the four-week-following window, with the sixteen-jurisdiction named-candidate cohort plus the UK and EU originating signatories each emitting attestations against the schema before end-Q3 2026, the cross-orchestrator interop matrix shipping general-availability with the schema as a default field, and the United States recognition gap still keyed to the FMRB executive order's signing path running on its own clock. Bear case is one or two member-state submissions deferring into a post-plenary written-procedure round, pushing formal Recommendation adoption into early Q4 2026 with first-cohort attestation emission still landing inside Q3; absent that slip, Q3 2026 lands the OECD GENAI reciprocity attestation schema adopted with the sixteen-jurisdiction perimeter operationalizing it as default.

reasoning.because: OECD GENAI member-state schema-comment submissions clear four-fifths with comment-close Friday May 29.
reasoning.given: Sixteen named candidates plus UK and EU; vendor interop matrix targets early-June GA with default support.
reasoning.so_that: The reciprocity attestation field schema adopts as an OECD Recommendation operationalized across the cohort.
reasoning.landing: By Q3 2026; sixteen jurisdictions plus UK and EU emit attestations against the schema.
reasoning.plain_language: Sixteen countries plus the UK and EU are about to agree on one shared way for AI tools to prove they meet safety rules, ready to use this summer.

summary: Wednesday's OECD GENAI procedural note clears four-fifths of member-state schema comments with the Friday May 29 close ahead of the June 2-6 plenary, the named-candidate cohort moves to sixteen with Brunei joining, and the cross-orchestrator interop matrix targets early-June GA with default schema support. By Q3 2026 the schema adopts as an OECD Recommendation.
